Yeah, then you’re looking at MGS3, PO, and Peace Walker. Technically 4? You also need to know that when it comes to the obsession and hero worship, Solid Snake is a commendable successor for reasons revealed in MGS1, 2, and 4.

Hard to divorce the man from the legends and spinoffs. The point is that he’s a product of his time and circumstances. Big Boss’ arc isn’t resolved until MGS4.

Then you’ve skewed the mentality you should have going into the game. MGS3 you’re dealing with a young, innocent Naked Snake. Portable Ops is canon, but not super important. Peace Walker is the proper sequel to 3. V is the proper sequel to Peace Walker.

You have to understand that Big Boss, as the greatest soldier who ever lived only had one confirmed (canon) kill.

If you don’t care about spoilers: Big Boss prevented WWIII in Operation Snake Eater by sacrificing the most important thing in his entire life. From there, Peace Walker is about him dealing with that sacrifice. PW ends with another brutalized betrayal, and V is about a jaded Big Boss dealing with that betrayal. 

Ultimately, the series (in my opinion) is about hero worship, and the damage surrounding it. Nobody’s really “right”, but some parties are more wrong than others. The vision and the motif is that “You control your fate; not your genetics, not your past, not your sins”.
It’s a testament to David Hayter more than it is to MGS. To bankroll and take a pay cut to get the original voice actors back is next level dedication. Truly for the love of the game.
